en.headline: Bar Association broadly backs new persistent child sexual abuse offence
en.dek: The legal body said it supports introducing a dedicated offence while calling for safeguards to ensure fair trials, and also urged expanded pre-conviction anonymity for both complainants and defendants.
body: The Hong Kong Bar Association said it broadly supports the introduction of a dedicated offence of persistent child sexual abuse, reversing earlier reservations expressed when the idea was last examined more than two decades ago.

Vice-chairman Martin Hui said the association agreed the offence reflected experience in other jurisdictions, but four safeguards were needed to protect fairness for both defendants and victims. These included prioritising specific substantive charges such as rape when evidence allows, and restricting the use of the persistent offence alongside or in place of specific charges.

In its response to the Security Bureau’s consultation on reforming sexual offence laws, the Bar Association also recommended extending pre-conviction anonymity protections to defendants as well as complainants, and supported a statutory definition of consent. The consultation period ended earlier this week.

zh.headline: 大律師公會原則支持新增持續性侵犯兒童罪
zh.dek: 公會回應性罪行法例諮詢，原則同意增設相關罪行但須設保障措施確保公平審訊，並倡擴大定罪前匿名保護。
body: 香港大律師公會就完善性罪行法例諮詢提交回應，原則上同意新增「持續性侵犯兒童」罪，認為反映其他司法管轄區過去二十多年經驗，惟須同時加設保障措施，確保審訊公平。
公會副主席許紹庭表示，若證據足以支持獨立實質控罪如強姦，控方應優先提出該等控罪，而非僅控持續侵犯罪；亦不應同時就同一行為控以持續罪及實質罪，或在舉證完結後申請改控。
公會另建議將定罪前匿名保護擴大至被告人及申訴人，以減低偏見；並支持為「同意」訂立法定定義。諮詢期已於本周較早前結束，保安局表示會積極考慮相關意見。
